thread:
sam: FYI PR #485 gpu-smoke shard-12 is red in nightly, failing on an H100 with `invalid device function`. Can someone quick-triage? CI link: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/485/12 :eyes:

ci-bot: job failed — https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/485/12 • artifacts: /artifacts/485/12/logs.tar.gz

alex: can you paste the kernel/log snippet and the CUDA/driver versions? quick check: `nvidia-smi` + `cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version`

sam: pasted logs below — failing pretty early in warmup.
```
[03:12:04][gpu-0] ERROR cuLaunchKernel: invalid device function
[03:12:04][gpu-0] CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_DEVICE_FUNCTION (code 8)
Xid 31
stacktrace: launching attention kernel -> nvfuser -> cuLaunchKernel
container runtime CUDA: 11.8
host driver reported by job: 520.61.05
model config: seq=256, bs=8
note: this cluster node is labeled `h100-canary-2`
```

maria: hm looks like a runtime/driver skew — container CUDA 11.8 vs host driver 520.x might be okay usually, but the kernel says invalid device function which often points to PTX/SM mismatch or a kernel compiled for a different arch. Any chance the image got rebuilt with newer kernels/flags? :thinking:

alex: also check the loaded kernel module version — run `nvidia-smi -q | head` and `strings /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 | grep "NVRM version"` if you can. If the host driver is older/newer than the libcuda used at compile-time that can cause `invalid device function`.

sam: ran those quickly on the failing node:
```
$ nvidia-smi
Sat Mar 15 03:10:58 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 520.61.05    Driver Version: 520.61.05    CUDA Version: 12.2     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
$ cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module  520.61.05  Wed Jan 20 2026
```

maria: ok host driver 520 + libcuda tied to 520, but container runtime is 11.8. The kernel complaining could be due to a new fused kernel that expects newer PTX from CUDA 12+ builds. Did we recently land any kernel codegen changes? @alex any suspects in the last 2 commits on the runtime branch?

alex: I did a small change to attention kernel lowering last week — it added a conditional for sm_90 intrinsics. It should be guarded by runtime-detected arch, but if the build artifact ended up compiled with sm_90-only code path due to a CI build container mismatch that could cause invalid device function on some images.

jordan: I can rerun the failing shard on the canary pool pinned to driver 515 (older) and on a node with the image built from the pinned CUDA 12 toolchain to compare. Want me to kick off two reruns and a quick bisect across commits 7f9.. -> b2a..?

sam: yes please. Also can we capture the exact `cuobjdump --list-elf` from the container image to see what PTX/archs are present? If kernel only has sm_90 SASS then older devices will error.

jordan: got it — kicking reruns now and uploading artifacts. Rerun jobs: https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/485/12/rerun-1 (driver-515), https://ci.redwood.ai/jobs/485/12/rerun-2 (cuda12-built-image). Bisect job queued: https://ci.redwood.ai/bisect/485

ci-bot: rerun jobs started — rerun-1 id=485-12-9001, rerun-2 id=485-12-9002. Artifacts will appear under /artifacts/485/12/reruns/

alex: thanks. If rerun-2 (cuda12-built) passes and original fails, that points to build-time ABI/codegen mismatch. If both fail, likely runtime/driver regression.

maria: if it's build mismatch we should label the PR and the failing CI as `flake:build-arch` and add an automated check to verify PTX targets in future. Also add a TODO to pin the runtime image for nightly GPUs until we stabilize.

sam: agreed — tagging this thread `flake:needs-rerun` and `investigate:codegen`. Assigning to @jordan to finish the bisect and to @alex for a patch if needed. :thumbsup:

jordan: will update the bisect timeline in the bisect job, aim to have initial verdict in 2 hours and a recommended rollback if bisect shows a recent change.

alex: quick note for reviewers — if you're running local repros, set `--target-sm=90,80` when building kernels to surface missing arch support early.

sam: thanks all. I'll wait for rerun artifacts and then create the issue if bisect lands on runtime change. :white_check_mark:
